bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta.issue_description / staged vulnerable source snapshot / saved sanitizer trace
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced a MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value in `SGIImage::readImage`. The staged 516-byte SGI/RGB witness passes `RGBHandler::canRead`, and `readImage` decodes `_rle = 1`, `_dim = 2`, `_xsize = 32`, `_ysize = 32`, `_zsize = 1`, and `_colormap = 0`, so it enters the RLE image path and derives `_numrows = _ysize * _zsize = 32`. In that path the code allocates `_starttab = new quint32[_numrows]` and fills it with `for (l = 0; !_stream.atEnd() && l < _numrows; l++)`. Because the witness is only 516 bytes long, exactly one 32-bit word remains after the 512-byte SGI header, so only `_starttab[0]` is read and normalized while `_starttab[1..31]` remain uninitialized. The vulnerable source then allocates `_lengthtab`, drains the remaining payload, and immediately runs the RLE sanity check `if (_starttab[o] + _lengthtab[o] > (uint)_data.size())` across all 32 rows. On the first unread tail entry the condition reads `_starttab[o]` from uninitialized heap storage, and MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `src/imageformats/rgb.cpp:352`. The staged fix adds a post-loop fill that zeroes every unread `_starttab` element before the sanity check.

source.description: First project-side read that materializes the attacker-controlled compression mode used by the vulnerable RLE-table path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` starts with SGI header bytes `01 da 01 01`. After `RGBHandler::canRead()` rewinds the `QBuffer`, this statement consumes the header's compression byte and sets `_rle = 1`, which is the only mode that allocates and later checks `_starttab`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: RLE sanity-check expression that reads `_starttab[o]` for every expected row even when EOF left the tail of `_starttab` uninitialized.
sink.note: The saved MSAN trace reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `src/imageformats/rgb.cpp:352:17` in this expression and attributes the poisoned bytes to the earlier `_starttab` heap allocation at line 334.

root_cause.description: The EOF-bounded fill loop initializes only the prefix of `_starttab`; the vulnerable source performs no post-loop initialization for unread entries before later consuming all `_numrows` slots.
root_cause.note: The staged patch adds `for (; l < _numrows; l++) { _starttab[l] = 0; }` immediately after this loop, confirming that the missing obligation is to define every unread `_starttab` element before the sanity check.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSAN origin. This heap allocation creates `_numrows` start-table entries with indeterminate contents; only entries overwritten by the subsequent stream-read loop become defined.
tainted_value_origin.note: The sanitizer's origin section records `operator new[]` followed by `SGIImage::readImage` at line 334.

parser_admitted.description: Format sniffing admits the witness as an SGI/RGB image before the handler rewinds the buffer and calls `SGIImage::readImage()`.
parser_admitted.note: The staged PoC begins with `01 da 01 01`, so `canRead()` returns true. Because the device is a non-sequential `QBuffer`, line 709 seeks back to the original position before `handler->read(&i)` reaches the vulnerable parser.

fine_trace.note: Reads the attacker-controlled compression flag from the SGI header. In the staged witness this becomes `_rle = 1`, so the later `if (_rle)` block is taken instead of the verbatim-image path.

Materializes the image dimensions and channel count from the same header. For the witnessed file `_xsize = 32`, `_ysize = 32`, and `_zsize = 1`; the later bug uses `_ysize` and `_zsize` to decide how many RLE table entries must exist.
Derives the expected RLE table length. With `_ysize = 32` and `_zsize = 1`, the parser expects 32 start offsets and 32 length entries.

Allocates a 32-entry heap array for row start offsets. `new[]` leaves every element indeterminate until the file-backed loop overwrites it. The staged file still has four bytes left after the 512-byte header, so the earlier `if (_stream.atEnd()) return false;` check does not stop execution before this allocation.

The fill loop stops when either all 32 entries are read or the stream reaches EOF. The staged file is 516 bytes long, so after the 512-byte header only one 32-bit word remains: `0x00000300`. That initializes `_starttab[0]`, which normalizes to `0` after subtracting `512 + _numrows * 2 * sizeof(quint32) = 768`, then EOF stops the loop at `l = 1`. Because the vulnerable source has no post-loop fill, `_starttab[1..31]` remain uninitialized.

The RLE sanity check iterates `o` from `0` to `_numrows - 1` and evaluates `_starttab[o] + _lengthtab[o]` for every row. After the initialized first entry, the next unread tail entry makes this expression read `_starttab[o]` from the heap storage left undefined by step 5. MemorySanitizer reports that read at line 352 and points back to the allocation in step 4.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The poisoned bytes come from the `_starttab` allocation at line 334, while the logical bug is the later EOF-bounded read loop that leaves unread `_starttab` entries undefined before the sanity check consumes them.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds `for (; l < _numrows; l++) { _starttab[l] = 0; }` immediately after the `_starttab` fill loop, so the sanity check no longer reads unread heap entries.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_14446 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which produced `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `SGIImage::readImage`.

format.name: SGI RLE RGB image
format.contract: The staged PoC is the exact 516-byte SGI/RGB blob in `gt_results/arvo_14446/poc`. Its trigger semantics are limited to the witnessed header and file length: bytes 0-3 are `01 da 01 01`, so `RGBHandler::canRead` accepts the format; the main header decodes `_dim = 2`, `_xsize = 32`, `_ysize = 32`, `_zsize = 1`, and `_colormap = 0`; and the file ends after exactly one 32-bit word beyond the 512-byte header. That lone word is `0x00000300`, which normalizes to `_starttab[0] = 0`, but the remaining 31 `_starttab` entries are never read from the file before the later sanity-check loop consumes `_starttab[o]` for all 32 rows. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader input class beyond this exact layout.
